arxiv-2104-11302.title: α \alpha -Firmly Nonexpansive Operators on Metric Spaces
arxiv-2104-11302.creator: Arian Bërdëllima, Florian Lauster, D. Russell Luke
arxiv-2104-11302.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arian Bërdëllima, Florian Lauster, D. Russell Luke. We extend to p p -uniformly convex spaces tools from the analysis of fixed point iterations in linear spaces. This study is restricted to an appropriate generalization of single-valued, pointwise α \alpha -averaged mappings. Our main contribution is establishing a calculus for these mappings in p-uniformly convex spaces, showing in particular how the property is preserved under compositions and convex combinations.

arxiv-2107-14438.title: Where are 3 ​ P 3P and higher P − P- wave states in the charmonium family?
arxiv-2107-14438.creator: Ming-Xiao Duan 1,2, Xiang Liu 1,2,3
arxiv-2107-14438.description: Abstract How to hunt for higher P P -wave states of charmonium is still an open topic when 2 ​ P 2P charmonia were identified. In this work, we present an unquenched quark model calculation to illustrate the spectroscopy behavior of these 3 ​ P 3P , 4 ​ P 4P and 5 ​ P 5P states in charmonium family.

arxiv-2203-16185.title: Reshaping the Jaynes-Cummings ladder with Majorana bound states
arxiv-2203-16185.creator: L. S. Ricco, V. K. Kozin, A. C. Seridonio, I. A. Shelykh
arxiv-2203-16185.description: Abstract We study the optical properties of a hybrid device composed by a quantum dot (QD) resonantly coupled to a photonic mode of an optical microcavity and a Majorana nanowire: a topological superconducting segment hosting Majorana bound states (MBSs) at the opposite ends.

arxiv-2404-02192.title: Integer and fractional quantum anomalous Hall effects in pentalayer graphene
arxiv-2404-02192.creator: Ming Xie, Sankar Das Sarma
arxiv-2404-02192.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ming Xie, Sankar Das Sarma. We critically analyze the recently reported observation of integer (IQAHE) and fractional (FQAHE) quantum anomalous Hall effects at zero applied magnetic field in pentalayer graphene. Our quantitative activation and variable range hopping transport analysis of the experimental data reveals that the observed IQAHE and FQAHE at different fillings all have similar excitation gaps of the order of 5 5 K − 10 -10 K.

arxiv-2410-09411.description: Abstract In-context learning (ICL) has emerged as a powerful capability for large language models (LLMs) to adapt to downstream tasks by leveraging a few (demonstration) examples. arxiv-2411-17079.title: Zero-Order Control Barrier Functions for Sampled-Data Systems with State and Input Dependent Safety Constraints
arxiv-2411-17079.creator: Xiao Tan ⋆, Ersin Daş ⋆, Aaron D. Ames, Joel W. Burdick
arxiv-2411-17079.description: Abstract We propose a novel zero-order control barrier function (ZOCBF) for sampled-data systems to ensure system safety. Our formulation generalizes conventional control barrier functions and straightforwardly handles safety constraints with high-relative degrees or those that explicitly depend on both system states and inputs. The proposed ZOCBF condition does not require any differentiation operation.

arxiv-2504-11038.title: QAVA: Query-Agnostic Visual Attack to Large Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2504-11038.creator: Yudong Zhang, Ruobing Xie, Jiansheng Chen, Xingwu Sun, Zhanhui Kang, Yu Wang, Technology Beijing, Faculty of Science, Technology, University of Macau
arxiv-2504-11038.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yudong Zhang, Ruobing Xie, Jiansheng Chen, Xingwu Sun, Zhanhui Kang, Yu Wang, Technology Beijing, Faculty of Science, Technology, University of Macau. In typical multimodal tasks, such as Visual Question Answering (VQA), adversarial attacks targeting a specific image and question can lead large vision-language models (LVLMs) to provide incorrect answers. However, it is common for a single image to be associated with multiple questions, and LVLMs may still answer other questions correctly even for an adversarial image attacked by a specific question.

arxiv-2510-17480.title: Unified Privacy Guarantees for Decentralized Learning via Matrix Factorization
arxiv-2510-17480.creator: Aurélien Bellet, Edwige Cyffers, Davide Frey, Romaric Gaudel, Dimitri Lerévérend, François Taïani
arxiv-2510-17480.description: Abstract Decentralized Learning (DL) enables users to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data by iteratively averaging local updates with neighbors in a network graph. This setting is increasingly popular for its scalability and its ability to keep data local under user control.

arxiv-2510-26822.title: Joint Optimization of Microphone Array Geometry, Sensor Directivity Pattern, and Beamforming Parameters for Linear Superarrays
arxiv-2510-26822.creator: Yuanhang Qian, Xueqin Luo, Jilu Jin, Gongping Huang, Jingdong Chen, Jacob Benesty
arxiv-2510-26822.description: Abstract Linear superarrays (LSAs) have been proposed to address the limited steering capability of conventional linear differential microphone arrays (LDMAs) by integrating omnidirectional and directional microphones, enabling more flexible beamformer designs. However, existing approaches remain limited because array geometry and element directivity, both critical to beamforming performance, are not jointly optimized.

pmc-11799291.title: Thymus and activation-regulated chemokine (CCL17) as a clinical biomarker in atopic dermatitis: significance and limitations in the new treatment era
pmc-11799291.creator: Yoko Kataoka
pmc-11799291.description: Thymus and activation-regulated chemokine (TARC; CCL17) is a T-helper-2 chemokine that reflects atopic dermatitis (AD) disease activity. Since 2008, serum TARC levels have been commercially measured in Japan, and clinical experience has shown the usefulness of TARC. The fallacy that eczema is always visible often hinders successful treatment, when there is subclinical inflammation which is inferable from the TARC level.

pmc-12418917.title: Insights From Language‐Trained Apes: Brain Network Plasticity and Communication
pmc-12418917.creator: Begun Erbaba, Mira Sinha, Elaine E. Guevara, Erin E. Hecht, William D. Hopkins, Chet C. Sherwood
pmc-12418917.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Language is central to the cognitive and sociocultural traits that distinguish humans, yet the evolutionary emergence of this capacity is far from fully understood. This review explores how the study of the brains of language‐trained apes (LTAs) offers a unique and valuable opportunity to tease apart the relative contribution of evolved species differences, behavior, and environment in the emergence of complex communication abilities.
